title: Regional firebreak and soft-shear degrader hotpatch
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: A regional capacity blip (2026-02-09 18:14 UTC) exposed a cascade in the soft-failover logic where rapid reconnects and aggressive occupant rejoin attempts caused disproportionate KV-cache pressure and node thrashing. This led to elevated tail latency and an increased rate of tenant-level SLO violations for a small subset of heavy customers. Motivation: Introduce a fast, reversible "firebreak" that temporarily enforces conservative ingress for affected regions while gracefully shedding load within tenant cohorts and preserving KV consistency. Goals: (1) Prevent oscillating rejoin cycles from overwhelming nodes, (2) ensure tenants receive deterministic degradation (soft-shear) rather than random termination, (3) retain telemetry hooks for post-incident analysis and automated rollback. Changes: - Introduce regional_firebreak controller that detects a sustained uplink surge beyond configured SLO breach thresholds and flips an ephemeral region-level hold with an exponential cool-down. - Soft-shear degrader applied at tenant-cohort level: instead of hard-drop, requests are probabilistically delayed or redirected to compatible lower-cost variants (quantized or smaller sequence-length models) depending on tenant policy. - Connection rejoin pacing: per-connection token bucket prevents aggressive reconnection loops; we persist a lightweight reconnect_timestamp to reduce duplicate inflight attempts. - KV preserver fence: when firebreak engages, we mark a short-lived read-priority on KV shards (read-through) to avoid thrashing background syncs during shutdown windows. - Telemetry/alerts: new metric region_firebreak_active{region} and tenant_soft_shear_rate with associated alerting rule tuned to avoid noisy escalation. - Config knobs exposed via runtime flags and Redwood Console feature flag for emergency enable/disable. Compatibility & safety: - Firebreak is reversible and defaults to a non-destructive monitoring mode. - All changes gate behind a runtime flag and an emergency rate limit profile that ops can toggle remotely. - Tight unit and integration coverage added for reconnect pacing and probabilistic routing. Checklist: - [x] Implements region_firebreak controller with unit tests. - [x] Adds soft-shear routing logic and policy config. - [x] Adds telemetry counters and alerting rule. - [x] Adds e2e scenario sim that reproduces rejoin storm locally. - [x] Smoke-tested on canary region (eu-west-1) with synthetic load. - [x] Ops runbook entry and rollback steps documented. Related: SUP-4421 (customer incident), ENG-2149 (work item). Testing notes: Unit tests added for pacing bucket, probabilistic decision boundaries and KV preserve fence. Integration test simulates 800 concurrent reconnects and verifies node stability with firebreak engaged vs disabled. Observed tail-99 latency reduced by ~45% in simulated scenario and tenant error rate lowered to baseline. Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind feature flag; 2) Canary enable in us-east-1 for 1hr under synthetic load; 3) Progressive 10% region enablement for 4 hours with telemetry gating; 4) Full enable if metrics stable. Hotpatch justification: This PR contains an emergency mitigation for a recently observed cascade; it is conservative, feature-flagged and designed for quick revert if unexpected regressions appear.

review_comments:
Diego Alvarez: Can we make the reconnect bucket size and refill configurable per-cluster? Ops will need this knob.
Maya Chen: Yes — added cluster-level override and documented the safe defaults.

Priya Natarajan: The probabilistic downgrade to smaller model variants needs a policy priority to avoid downgrading critical customers.
Maya Chen: Added tenant policy tag 'critical=false/true' and criticals are excluded from automatic downgrade; only subject to delay-based damping.

Ethan Cole: Did CI catch the flaky e2e? I saw a transient failure on the first run.
Maya Chen: The first run failed due to timing sensitivity of the synthetic harness; adjusted test to poll for stability and retried. CI now passes.
QA Bot: Integration smoke failed on first run (timing), rerun succeeded.
merge_decision: Merged after two approvals and CI green; feature gated. Ops performed canary enable in eu-west-1 post-merge.
release_notes: Hotpatch: Introduced region-level firebreak and tenant soft-shear degrader to stabilize nodes during reconnect/rejoin storms. Feature-flagged; canary release performed. See ENG-2149/SUP-4421 for incident details.
notes_for_ops: Emergency runbook added at docs/ops/firebreak-runbook.md. To disable firebreak globally: toggle feature flag 'region_firebreak.enabled=false' in Console or run 'redwoodctl feature disable region_firebreak'. For immediate rollback revert the feature flag and restart controller pods gracefully. Monitor metrics region_firebreak_active and tenant_soft_shear_rate and check KV shard sync lag.
notes: This PR was deployed as an emergency hotpatch. No database migrations. The change is low-risk and reversible; telemetry will be monitored for 72h post-rollout.
